resources.string: Screen recognition finds buttons, text and other elements that apps and games draw without making them accessible. SandFly shows them as items that you can swipe to and double-tap.
To recognise the current screen, open the SandFly menu and choose Recognise screen.

To recognise every screen of an app, open the app, open the SandFly menu, and choose Turn on screen recognition. To see the apps with automatic recognition, go to Settings, SandFly Pro, Automatic screen recognition.
Screen recognition is part of SandFly Pro. To buy SandFly Pro or enter a code, go to Settings, SandFly Pro.

You can choose a keymap for a physical keyboard: SandFly, VoiceOver, NVDA, JAWS or Orca. The VoiceOver, NVDA, JAWS and Orca keymaps use the shortcuts of those screen readers. Go to Settings, Keyboard shortcuts, Choose a keymap. To make your own keymap from the current one, choose New keymap.

Each keymap has its own SandFly key, the key that you hold down for SandFly shortcuts. Go to Settings, Keyboard shortcuts, Choose SandFly key. The list shows only the keys that keep every shortcut of the keymap.
You can assign different commands to keyboard shortcuts in one app. Go to Settings, Keyboard shortcuts, Keyboard shortcuts in apps, and choose the app.
You can assign any shortcut to Turn browse mode on or off, including pressing the SandFly key twice. Go to Settings, Keyboard shortcuts.

Some apps and games use keys that SandFly uses without the SandFly key, such as the arrow keys. To send these keys to the current app, use Pass keys without the SandFly key to this app. To stop, use the command again.
The keyboard tutorial is now interactive, like the touch tutorial. You press each shortcut, and SandFly checks it. Go to Settings, Help and feedback, SandFly tutorial, Keyboard tutorial.

In these keymaps, you use the keys as on a computer, without the SandFly key. Down Arrow and Up Arrow move to the next or previous item. Left Arrow and Right Arrow move by character, and Ctrl with Left Arrow or Right Arrow moves by word. Tab and Shift + Tab move to the next or previous item that can take focus. Enter activates the item, and Escape goes back. In a text field, these keys type and move the cursor as usual.

Object navigation moves through items in the way they are nested on the screen: to the object that contains the current item, to the first object inside it, and to the next or previous object. The commands are in Settings, Commands, Object navigation.
With the review cursor, you can read the screen by line, word and character without moving SandFly focus, and click or long-click at the cursor. The commands are in Settings, Commands, Screen review.
Recognise text on screen reads all the text on the screen, including text in pictures. Use the review cursor to move through the text, and press Escape to close it.

With gesture profiles, you can switch between sets of commands for your gestures. To create one, go to Settings, Gestures, Gesture profiles, and choose Add gesture profile. To change the profile, use Next gesture profile or Previous gesture profile, the Gesture profile reading control, or the SandFly menu.
You can assign different commands to gestures in one app. Go to Settings, Gestures, Gestures in apps, and choose the app.

Each one-finger swipe also has a swipe and hold: swipe, keep your finger still at the end, then lift it. You can assign a command to each one in Settings, Gestures. To change how long you hold, go to Settings, Gestures, Hold time after a swipe.
Tap to activate navigation bar buttons
To activate the buttons in the navigation bar with one tap, go to Settings, Touch, and turn on Tap to activate navigation bar buttons. This setting is separate from Lift to activate.
You can change how text is spoken, in all apps or in one app. Go to Settings, Speech, Speech dictionary, and choose Add a replacement.
Apps can ask to speak text with SandFly speech. To allow or stop an app, go to Settings, Speech, Let other apps speak. The current keyboard app can speak without asking.

After a call, Android can keep sending speech to the earpiece. To move SandFly speech back, go to Settings, Audio output, and turn on Reset accessibility audio after calls. This setting needs Shizuku.
SandFly has new sounds, and every sound has a vibration. A gesture that does nothing plays two short falling notes. You can still replace the sounds with a sound theme.

Type an app\'s name in braille to open it turns the screen into a braille keyboard. Type the first letters of the app name in uncontracted braille. To move between the apps that match, swipe down or up with one finger. To open the app, swipe up with two fingers. To close, swipe down with two fingers.
You can now use Japanese braille. The Japanese dictionary downloads the first time you use it. To choose Japanese, go to Languages in the braille keyboard settings or the braille display settings.
Braille keyboard with a physical keyboard

While a physical keyboard is connected, the braille keyboard is hidden, like other on-screen keyboards. It stays on screen while a braille display is connected, or when Use on-screen keyboard is on in Android settings.
To assign these commands to a gesture or a keyboard shortcut, go to Settings, Commands.
Sends the text in the current text field, with the send button next to it or the action key on the keyboard, such as Send or Search.

Lists the text that you copied, newest first, to copy again or remove. While Shizuku allows SandFly, text that you copy in other apps is added too. Passwords and other text marked sensitive are not added. Add to clipboard adds text after the text already on the clipboard.
Turns Android screen magnification on or off.
Move back or forward in the media that is playing.
Run the accessibility shortcut of another feature, such as Reading mode. These commands need Shizuku.
Taps the screen where the current item is, for items that do nothing when SandFly activates them.
Stops the notification that SandFly is reading, also in the voice of a voice profile.

Scripts can now touch the screen, press keys, run SandFly commands, open windows with rows, headings and sliders, recognise text, and speak during calls. Before you install a script, SandFly shows where it comes from and whether SandFly signed it.
Some phones stop background apps to save battery. To keep SandFly running, go to Settings, Display, and choose Use SandFly as the wallpaper. To choose the picture, use Wallpaper image.
